---
title: "Tips in a Shiny app"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Tips can talk to your server. Your app can learn which tip a reader pinned, open or rewrite a tip from an observer, show
the reason a button is switched off, and draw a plot inside a tip only while it is open.

Each example below is a complete app: paste it into R and run it. The module snippet at the end is the exception.

## Let the reader keep a tip open

Give the tag `pin = TRUE` and an `id`. The tip gets a small pin button, and the `P` key pins it too. A pinned tip stays
until the reader closes it, so they can read it while they work.

`events = "pin"` sends what happened to the server, as `input$<id>_pin`.

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(hovercraft)

ui <- fluidPage(
  tip_on(
    actionButton("run", "Run"),
    "Runs the **check** on every dataset",
    pin = TRUE,
    events = "pin",
    id = "run"
  ),
  textOutput("state")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$state <- renderText({
    if (is.null(input$run_pin)) "Nothing pinned yet" else paste("The tip is", input$run_pin$state)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

`state` is `"pinned"` when the reader pins the tip and `"closed"` when it closes, and `reason` says why it closed. A third
value, `"updated"`, means an already pinned tip was drawn again with new content, so test for `state == "pinned"` rather
than for anything that is not `"closed"`. The input is `NULL` until the first event.

One pin stays open at a time. To keep more, set `use_hovercraft(max_pins = 3)` once in the page's UI.

`events = "hint"` reports the tip that shows on hover or focus, as `input$<id>_hint`: `state` is `"shown"` or `"hidden"`, and
`reason` says why it closed. Use it when the app needs to know what a reader looked at, not what they kept. Events are off
unless you ask for them, because `"hint"` sends a message to the server every time a tip opens or closes.

## Open and change a tip from the server

`tip_show()`, `tip_hide()` and `tip_update()` find the tip by its `id`.

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(hovercraft)

ui <- fluidPage(
  tip_on(actionButton("run", "Run"), "Runs the **check**", id = "run"),
  actionButton("help", "Show me"),
  actionButton("done", "Mark as done")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$help, tip_show("run"))
  observeEvent(input$done, tip_update("run", text = "The check **finished**"))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

`tip_update()` takes `text`, `template`, `record` and `placement`. Leave one out and it stays as it is; `NA` takes it
away. Two rules: a `template` given without `text` also drops the old plain text, because plain text beats a template,
and a `record` needs a `template` (or `text` with placeholders) in the same call. An open tip draws the new words at once.

`tip_hide()` closes a tip that shows on hover or focus, or one opened with `tip_show()`. It never closes a pin, and no
server call pins a tip. A tip opened with `tip_show()` also closes when the reader clicks away, opens another tip or presses
Escape.

## Say why a button is off

A switched-off button gets no pointer and no keyboard focus, so it cannot show a tip. Give `when_disabled` the reason, and
the tip says "Not available:" and the reason, with a small lock.

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(hovercraft)

ui <- fluidPage(
  tip_on(
    actionButton("submit", "Submit"),
    "Sends the form",
    when_disabled = "Fill in every required field first"
  ),
  checkboxInput("ready", "Everything is filled in", FALSE)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observe(updateActionButton(session, "submit", disabled = !input$ready))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

When the button is switched on again, the reason goes and the tip is the normal one. hovercraft wraps a disabled control
in a small element that can take the pointer and the keyboard, since the control itself cannot. The `tip_on()` help page
lists what is not covered: a control directly inside a `btn-group`, `btn-group-vertical` or `input-group`, and one
disabled with `aria-disabled` alone.

## Put a live output in a tip

`tip_output()` puts a plot, a table or any other Shiny output inside a template. The output is drawn while the tip is
open, so a page with a hundred tips does not compute a hundred plots.

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(hovercraft)

ui <- fluidPage(
  tip_define(
    trend = tip_template(
      tip_title("{{ label }}"),
      tip_output(plotOutput("trend_plot", width = 260, height = 140))
    )
  ),
  tip_on(
    actionButton("adae", "ADAE"),
    template = "trend",
    record = list(label = "ADAE differences"),
    id = "adae"
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$trend_plot <- renderPlot({
    par(mar = c(2, 2, 1, 1))
    plot(c(3, 5, 4, 8), type = "b")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

While the output computes, the tip shows a loading note. If the render fails, the tip shows the error with a Retry button.
Retry sets `input$<output>_retry`, so put that input on a line of its own at the top of the render: Shiny runs a render
again only when something it reads has changed.

One output has one place on the page. When several items share a template, the tip shows the output for the item that is
open. Your render learns which one by reading the `"hint"` input of the items (`events = "hint"`). The help page for
`tip_output()` has a worked example with two items.

## In modules

A template belongs to the whole page, so two copies of a module share one unless its name carries the module's namespace.

In a module's UI, give `ns()` to the `id` of `tip_on()`, to `tip_output()` and to the template's name. In its server, read
`input$<id>_pin` and call `tip_show()`, `tip_hide()` and `tip_update()` with the plain id, without the namespace.

```{r}
tip_define(!!ns("row") := tip_template(tip_title("{{ label }}")))
tip_on(htmltools::tags$tr(htmltools::tags$td("ADSL"), tabindex = "0"), template = ns("row"), record = list(label = "ADSL"))
```

## Where to go next

- Every function on this page has a section in [the book](the-book.html), with live figures and the inputs your server
  gets, shown as the reader acts.
- Tips on the rows of a `DT` or `reactable` table also pin and send events: see [Tips on tables](tables.html).
- The look of all of these is set in [Themes and looks](themes.html).

`tip_on(pin = TRUE)` with an `id` is stable. `events`, `when_disabled`, `tip_show()`, `tip_hide()`, `tip_update()`,
`tip_output()` and `use_hovercraft(max_pins = )` are experimental in 0.1.0 and may change in a later release. Each help page
says which part is which.
